source.title: Hormoni nisu izgovor: Što prehrana, stres i životne navike imaju s njima?

summary.title_hr: Hormoni nisu izgovor: Što prehrana, stres i životne navike imaju s njima?
summary.abstract_hr: U epizodi podcasta „Rastući s djecom” voditeljica Ana Pavlović razgovara s nutricionisticom Mirnom Sentić o tome kako san, stres, kofein i prehrambene navike utječu na hormone, posebno na inzulin, kortizol i spolne hormone. Mirna objašnjava ulogu inzulina kao hormona sitosti i slikovito opisuje uravnotežen tanjur na koji proteini, masti i ugljikohidrati gore poput cjepanice, pruća i papira. Velik dio razgovora posvećen je plodnosti, sekundarnoj neplodnosti i PCOS-u (koji Mirna naziva i PMOS), uz naglasak na tome da se taj sindrom ne može svesti samo na izgled jajnika i da je potreban ljudski pristup ženama. Govori se i o PMS-u, žudnjama za hranom, osjećaju krivnje nakon jela, balkanskoj „kulturi obilja” te o tome da nijedna namirnica sama po sebi nije loša. Razgovor završava porukom da se za savjet treba obratiti struci prije nego umjetnoj inteligenciji, a nastavak o nadutosti najavljen je za Patreon.
key_topics: odnos prema hrani i osjećaj krivnje
key_points: Mirna ističe da manjak sna i jutarnje kave bez obroka narušavaju prirodan ritam kortizola i inzulina, zbog čega smo kroz dan umorniji i gladniji. Kavu savjetuje piti uz obrok, a kao radikalni „reset” predlaže dva dana ranog ustajanja, odlaska na spavanje oko 22 sata i izbacivanja kofeina.

Za uravnotežen obrok koristi metaforu vatre: protein je cjepanica, masti su pruće, a ugljikohidrati papir. Predlaže tanjur podijeljen na trećine („Mercedes znak”), uz manji udio ugljikohidrata prema večeri kako bi se inzulin preko noći smirio.

Stres i kortizol, primjerice strah da trudnoća neće uspjeti ili egzistencijalne brige, mogu suprimirati ovulaciju. Kod sekundarne neplodnosti problem je najčešće hormonski „šum” koji je postojao i prije, a tijelo ga je u mlađoj dobi lakše nadišlo.

PCOS (koji Mirna naziva i PMOS, poliendokrinološki metabolički ovarijski sindrom) ne može se dijagnosticirati samo po izgledu jajnika ni po fizionomiji žene. Preporučuje provjeru inzulina (OGTT ili HOMA indeks), štitnjače i navika, a i sama s PCOS-om živi 15 godina.
Jači PMS povezuje s inzulinom i slabljenjem žutog tijela, odnosno nestabilnim progesteronom. U lutealnoj fazi preporučuje više proteina, a slatko jesti uz obrok, a ne samostalno.

Naglašava da nijedna namirnica (mlijeko, gluten, kruh, voće) nije sama po sebi loša te da treba razumjeti kontekst i potrebe osobe. Ističe i da krivnja nakon jela šteti, a osjećaj zadovoljstva hormonski bolje djeluje.
Poručuje da je ženama potreban ljudski pristup bez posramljivanja, da par čini obitelj i bez djece te da u pitanjima zdravlja treba pitati struku prije umjetne inteligencije.
key_topics_en: relationship with food and feeling of guilt
key_points_en: Mirna emphasizes that lack of sleep and morning coffees without a meal disrupt the natural rhythm of cortisol and insulin, which makes us more tired and hungrier throughout the day. She advises drinking coffee with a meal, and as a radical "reset" suggests two days of waking up early, going to bed around 10 PM, and eliminating caffeine.

For a balanced meal, she uses the metaphor of fire: protein is a log, fats are twigs, and carbohydrates are paper. She suggests a plate divided into thirds ("Mercedes sign"), with a lower proportion of carbohydrates toward the evening so that insulin settles down overnight.

Stress and cortisol, for example fear that a pregnancy will not succeed or existential worries, can suppress ovulation. In secondary infertility, the problem is most often hormonal "noise" that existed before as well, and the body overcame it more easily at a younger age.

PCOS (which Mirna also calls PMOS, polyendocrinological metabolic ovarian syndrome) cannot be diagnosed solely by the appearance of the ovaries or by a woman's physiognomy. She recommends checking insulin (OGTT or HOMA index), thyroid, and habits, and she herself has lived with PCOS for 15 years.

She links stronger PMS with insulin and the weakening of the corpus luteum, that is, unstable progesterone. In the luteal phase, she recommends more protein, and eating sweets with a meal, not independently.

She emphasizes that no food item (milk, gluten, bread, fruit) is bad in itself and that one must understand the context and needs of the person. She also points out that guilt after eating is harmful, while a feeling of satisfaction works better hormonally.

She conveys that women need a humane approach without shaming, that a couple constitutes a family even without children, and that in health matters one should ask the profession before artificial intelligence.
summary.title_en: Hormones Are Not an Excuse: What Do Nutrition, Stress, and Lifestyle Habits Have to Do with Them?
summary.abstract_en: In an episode of the podcast "Rastući s djecom", host Ana Pavlović talks with nutritionist Mirna Sentić about how sleep, stress, caffeine, and dietary habits affect hormones, especially insulin, cortisol, and sex hormones. Mirna explains the role of insulin as a satiety hormone and vividly describes a balanced plate on which proteins, fats, and carbohydrates burn like a log, twigs, and paper. A large part of the conversation is dedicated to fertility, secondary infertility, and PCOS (which Mirna also calls PMOS), emphasizing that this syndrome cannot be reduced solely to the appearance of the ovaries and that a humane approach to women is needed. They also talk about PMS, food cravings, feelings of guilt after eating, the Balkan "culture of abundance", and the fact that no food item is bad in itself. The conversation ends with a message that one should turn to the profession for advice before artificial intelligence, and a sequel about bloating was announced for Patreon.
